title: ITER Hands Over Vacuum Vessel Sector #3, Closing Three-Year Bevel Repair Campaign
detail: ITER's contractor SIMANN (SIMIC/Ansaldo Nucleare) officially handed over vacuum vessel sector #3 to the assembly team on September 2, 2026, after a summer of intensive work completing bevel repairs — the weld edges where sectors join to form the tokamak's plasma chamber — plus outer-shell instrumentation and inner-shell boss welding. Sector #3 carries 120 sensors for measuring magnetic field during operation. The handover closes a nearly three-year campaign that repaired dimensional irregularities in vacuum vessel bevels across all affected sectors, one of the defects that triggered the 2024 Baseline schedule revision.

title: Realta Fusion and Madison Gas and Electric Announce Partnership to Explore 200-MWe Wisconsin Fusion Plant
detail: Realta Fusion and Madison Gas and Electric (MGE) announced a strategic partnership on September 2, 2026 to jointly explore a 200-megawatt-electric, grid-connected fusion power plant in Wisconsin — among the first such utility-fusion partnerships in the US. MGE made a direct equity investment in Realta in this initial phase and committed equipment, engineering, and technical support plus assistance with siting, permitting, interconnection, and financing for the prospective plant. Realta's magnetic mirror prototype, Hammir, is under development at its new Realta Forge R&D headquarters at Madison's former Oscar Mayer site.

media.caption: Realta Fusion and MGE announce Wisconsin fusion plant partnership

title: Japan's METI Conditionally Selects Four Private Fusion Demonstration Projects for ¥60B in Subsidies
detail: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) conditionally selected four industry-led projects for its fusion power generation demonstration program, spanning laser, stellarator, field-reversed-configuration, and tokamak approaches: EX-Fusion (with Hamamatsu Photonics, laser fusion), Helical Fusion (stellarator, under its Helix Program), LINEA Innovation (beam-supported field-reversed configuration), and Starlight Engine (with Kyoto Fusioneering, HTS tokamak). The program provides roughly ¥60 billion (~$370M) in milestone-based government support through 2028, targeting fusion power demonstration in the 2030s; formal adoption is expected as early as October 2026.

media.caption: Japan METI selects four fusion demonstration projects
